subject: Vocational School Capital Skills Grant Match
overview: The City Council approved a $250,000 free-cash appropriation to match a state Capital Skills Grant for Medford Vocational Technical High School. The Council also passed resolutions regarding traffic mitigation at Wellington Circle, updates to the capital improvement plan, and creating civic advisory committees for development projects.

items.title: Vocational School Capital Skills Grant Match Appropriation
items.summary: Approved a $250,000 appropriation from certified free cash to serve as a matching grant for vocational programs in culinary arts, hospitality, and advanced manufacturing at Medford Vocational Technical High School.

items.title: Wellington Circle Traffic and Pedestrian Safety Update
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting an administration update on traffic improvements and pedestrian safety at Wellington Circle, the Fellsway, and Mystic Avenue, focusing on state audit recommendations and Wynn Casino mitigation commitments.

items.title: Updated Capital Improvement Plan Request
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that the administration provide the council with an updated draft of the Capital Improvement Plan within 30 days ahead of upcoming budget discussions.

items.title: National Grid Sidewalk Repair at 2500 Mystic Valley Parkway
items.summary: Approved a resolution asking the administration to direct National Grid Gas to immediately repair hazardous sidewalk conditions following a gas leak near Winthrop Street.

items.title: Civic Advisory Committees for Development Projects
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that the administration establish civic advisory committees composed of local residents to review proposed developments of four or more units.

items.title: Commendation and Condolence Resolutions
items.summary: Congratulated Brittany Lanzilli on winning a bronze medal at the Winter World University Games and offered condolences to the families of World War II veteran Arthur Ford and longtime DPW employee Philip Genta.
